questions.question: What do social and economic rights require the state to do?
options: Take positive action to ensure access to basic necessities
questions.explanation: Unlike civil rights (freedom from interference), social and economic rights require the state to take positive action.

questions.question: Which treaty primarily protects social and economic rights?
questions.explanation: Social and economic rights are enshrined in the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR).

questions.question: Why is education sometimes called a "multiplier right"?
options: It enables the enjoyment of all other rights
It is the only right that exists
It can be bought and sold
questions.explanation: Education is a "multiplier right" because it enables people to realise and exercise all their other rights.

questions.question: Who became a global symbol for the right to education after surviving an attack in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Malala Yousafzai, shot by the Taliban in 2012 for advocating girls' education, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014.

questions.question: What did the Vienna Declaration (1993) affirm about all human rights?
options: They are universal, indivisible, interdependent and interrelated
Civil rights are superior to economic rights
Economic rights are not real rights
questions.explanation: The Vienna Declaration (1993) affirmed that all rights are universal, indivisible, interdependent and interrelated.
